Senses.PreferredTarget: the young horse tramples everyone under heaven to death
SearchAliases: the young horse tramples everyone under heaven to death
Senses.Note: “Young horse” is the traditional epithet invoked for Mazu in the retained Chan passages; the trampling remains appraisal language, not a death report.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The “young horse” is Mazu: later appraisals and verses say he tramples everyone under heaven, sometimes linking the line to his “Zang’s head is white, Hai’s head is black” response or his shout.
EvidenceBody: The horse-colt epithet and trampling predicate recur together in verse and appraisal; the surrounding cases identify Mazu rather than an unnamed literal animal.
